# aarambh-studio v3.0.0

aarambh-studio v3.0.0 is the third production source release of the ground-up
Rust LLM application. It completes Phases 29–40 and delivers a new efficient
attention stack, fine-grained MoE, multi-token prediction, on-policy
distillation, native quantization-aware training, native video and document
understanding, long-horizon tool-use chains, forgetting diagnostics, and Max
thinking mode.

## Distribution Policy

- This is a GitHub source release of an application, not a crates.io library release.
- All 19 workspace packages remain `publish = false`. crates.io publishing is
  deferred to v4.0.0.
- GitHub's automatic source archives are the only release assets.
- No pretrained checkpoint, adapter, tokenizer, optimizer state, SafeTensors,
  GGUF file, or compiled CPU/CUDA binary is included.
- Users train, convert, fine-tune, quantise, and serve their own local checkpoints.

## v3 Highlights

### Efficient Attention Stack (Phases 29–30)

- **Gated DeltaNet** — hybrid linear attention interleaved with a minority of
  full-attention layers. Decayed delta-rule recurrence with causal depthwise
  q/k/v convolution, learned alpha/beta gates, and a constant-size recurrent
  state (no sequence-length-dependent KV allocation). Retrofitted onto existing
  pretrained checkpoints via continued pretraining.
- **DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)** — learned/scored block-sparse attention
  for the remaining full-attention layers. A lightweight lightning indexer
  selects the top-K key blocks per query before the expensive matmul, falling
  back to dense attention automatically on short sequences.
- Combined: the v3.0 default stack is mostly Gated DeltaNet, a minority of
  DSA-sparse layers, and zero fully-dense full-attention layers (dense remains
  available as a config fallback).

### Fine-Grained MoE With Shared Expert (Phase 31)

- Upgraded v2's dense-masked-matmul MoE to a fine-grained routing design:
  many small experts rather than few large ones, plus always-active shared
  experts every token passes through regardless of router decisions.
- Router warm-start initialises the finer-grained router from an already-trained
  v2 coarse router's weights where dimensions allow.
- Load-balancing auxiliary loss excludes the shared expert's fixed activation.

### Multi-Token Prediction (Phase 32)

- Lightweight auxiliary MTP heads predict multiple future tokens per position
  during training, giving a denser training signal per forward pass.
- MTP heads double as a free draft source for speculative decoding, avoiding the
  need for a separate small draft checkpoint.

### On-Policy Distillation (Phase 33)

- New `aarambh-studio-distill` crate: student generates on-policy rollouts scored
  by a larger teacher (or scored-reference dataset), reducing the
  train/inference distribution mismatch of offline distillation.
- KL-style and reward-style teacher scoring paths behind a shared trait.
- Blends with the MTP auxiliary loss where enabled.

### Native Quantization-Aware Training (Phase 34)

- Device-native FakeQuantize for INT4/INT8 with identity STE, no host tensor
  conversion in the training forward/backward path.
- ExportAligned mode exactly matches Q4_K_M blocks and global Q8 absmax.
- QAT wraps attention, FFN/expert, MoE-router, DeltaNet, DSA-indexer, and MTP
  projections; embeddings/norms/convolutions/scalars remain full precision.
- Post-QAT conversion reuses the existing GGUF exporter unchanged.

### Native Video & Document Understanding (Phases 35–36)

- **Video:** Native H.264 MP4 decoding through bundled OpenH264, deterministic
  uniform/scene-aware frame sampling, learned/sinusoidal temporal offsets, and
  shared VLM DoRA training reusing v2's frozen ViT encoder path.
- **Documents:** PDF page rasterisation through pure-Rust Hayro, layout-aware
  projection with 2D positional information per patch, multi-page support with
  `<page_sep>` tokens, and shared DoRA tuning (one training code path, three
  data types: image, video, document).
- New reserved tokens: `<video>`, `<video_end>`, `<frame_sep>`, `<document>`,
  `<document_end>`, `<page_sep>`.

### Long-Horizon Tool-Use Chains (Phase 37)

- New `aarambh-studio-agent` crate: multi-step tool chains that orchestrate
  repeated calls into the existing inference path, feeding each tool result
  back into context as the next turn's input.
- Typed `ToolResult` wrappers supporting text, image, video, and document
  results — chains can hand back "here is a screenshot" and have the next step
  reason over it natively.
- Explicit step budget (1–64), eviction/summarisation policy under context
  pressure, and multi-step SFT loss-masking across multi-turn transcripts.
- Still an emit/orchestrate boundary: tool execution remains the caller's
  responsibility.

### Forgetting Diagnostics (Phase 38)

- Persistent per-capability forgetting curves (math, code, reasoning, factual,
  vision, video, document, tool-use) measured across training checkpoints/steps.
- `CapabilityProbe` reuses the eval harness's existing task subsets as probes
  rather than inventing new benchmark data.
- MoE routing signatures captured per probe example as a separate routing-drift
  diagnostic.
- Shared JSONL export format directly importable by Manas's associative-memory
  anti-forgetting tracking — no runtime or filesystem dependency between the
  projects.

### Max Thinking Mode (Phase 39)

- Fifth `ThinkingMode::Max` variant with a 16,384-token nominal budget — the
  next step in the existing ~4x progression (0 → 256 → 1,024 → 4,096 → 16,384).
- Zero structural changes to `ThinkingController`: the same forced-token
  mechanism, budget tracking, and collapse-on-force-close behaviour every
  existing mode already has.
- Per-mode sampling defaults (Max: temperature 0.85, top_p 0.97) applied only
  when the caller omits explicit parameters.
- Centralised `none|low|medium|high|max` vocabulary shared by every CLI command,
  the serving API, GRPO, and distillation.
- `hard-problems` eval task for High-vs-Max accuracy comparison.
- `GrpoThinkingMode::Max` and `DistillThinkingMode::Max` with no reward-shaping
  or objective changes.

## Production Hardening

- Every package reports version `3.0.0`; `aarambh-studio --version` matches
  the tag.
- Rust 1.89 is the MSRV.
- `Cargo.lock` is committed and all CI/release commands use `--locked`.
- The release profile uses `opt-level=3`, Thin LTO, one codegen unit, and
  stripped debug info.
- Every exported Rust API is documented and `missing_docs` is denied.
- Every unsafe block has an explicit safety rationale and Clippy enforces it.
- The release audit rejects unfinished implementation markers, unchecked roadmap
  tasks, publishable packages, version drift, and tracked model artifacts.
- CI validates stable Rust, Rust 1.89, formatting, checks, Clippy, tests,
  rustdoc, release build, CLI coverage, shell syntax, and RustSec advisories.
- CI now also covers the `aarambh-studio-agent`, `aarambh-studio-distill` crates, the
  `agent`, `distill` CLI commands, and video/document/forgetting eval tasks.

## Install From Source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/AarambhDevHub/aarambh-studio.git
cd aarambh-studio
git checkout v3.0.0
cargo build --release -p aarambh-studio --locked
target/release/aarambh-studio --version
```

For a local Cargo installation from the checked-out source:

```sh
cargo install --path aarambh-studio --locked
aarambh-studio --version
```

## Compatibility

- Existing v1/v2 dense model configurations remain valid when v3-only fields
  (`attention_schedule`, `dsa_config`, `mtp`, `qat`) are absent.
- Existing v1/v2 tokenizer IDs and checkpoint paths remain supported.
- Existing LoRA/DoRA adapter merge and SafeTensors/GGUF inference paths remain
  available.
- v3.0.x is the supported release line; v2.0.x is no longer maintained.

## Known Boundaries

- No pretrained model quality claim is made because no weights are distributed.
- crates.io publishing is deferred to v4.0.0.
- Multi-GPU support is single-node NCCL; multi-node training is out of scope.
- MoE uses correctness-first dense masked dispatch rather than sparse grouped
  dispatch.
- The inference server is local/self-hosted and does not claim every OpenAI
  endpoint or parameter.
- CUDA throughput depends on the GPU, driver, toolkit, shape, and dtype;
  hardware timing is not a CI gate.
- Audio modality is not supported (video is visual frames only).

## Security

- Streaming and non-streaming requests pass through the configured safety policy.
- Non-loopback server binds require bearer authentication.
- Request bodies and queues are bounded, CORS is opt-in, and internal errors
  are sanitized.
- Safety audit logs store prompt hashes rather than raw prompts.
- Structured tool calls are validated and never executed by the inference engine.

See `CHANGELOG.md`, `ARCHITECTURE_V3.md`, `ROADMAP_V3.md`, and `RELEASE.md`
for the complete engineering history and release procedure.
